nodes.name: Kart rigid body
nodes.purpose: Per-update rigid body integration for every kart: box mass and inertia, gravity selection, accumulated force and torque, angular velocity solve and the pose write-back that places the model in the world

nodes.name: Kart contact resolution
nodes.purpose: What the body does when it touches something: ground impulse with tangential friction, wall and vertex reflection, object reflection and kart-versus-kart mass-weighted bouncing

nodes.name: Kart math utilities
nodes.purpose: Small linear algebra and smoothing set the kart code leans on: a Gaussian elimination solve for the contact mass matrix, a fast reciprocal square root, spherical-to-cartesian conversion through angle lookups, and the easing helpers used for every ramped value

nodes.name: Kart control manager
nodes.purpose: The static manager that owns every kart body and answers the queries the rest of the game needs: per-surface top speed, down-slope bonuses, water depth and the player-versus-partner controller split

nodes.name: Crash and spin states
nodes.purpose: Timed kart states entered when an item or hazard lands: full spin, half spin, bomb launch, tornado throw, burn and freeze, each with the angular ramp that carries the body through the state and back to driving

nodes.name: Star, thunder and damage states
nodes.purpose: Long-running kart buffs and debuffs: star invulnerability and its countdown, the thunder shrink-and-recover cycle, and the four damage reaction timers that lock a driver out of steering

nodes.name: Kart chase camera
nodes.purpose: Chooses which camera mode a view uses each update and places the chase, fixed, search and path cameras relative to the kart and to authored camera data

nodes.name: Kart and driver attribute tables
nodes.purpose: Per-driver and per-vehicle attribute records: driver weight class, default partner and default vehicle, plus per-vehicle weight class and wheel count, all reached through lookup switches

nodes.name: Race manager
nodes.purpose: Owns the race frame: stage ordering for the physics and object updates, the ranking pass for every race and battle mode, and the start-grid placement handed to the karts

nodes.name: Lap and sector tracking
nodes.purpose: Converts a kart's world position into fractional progress between checkpoint planes, accumulates that into race progress and decides laps, goals, shortcuts and reverse driving

nodes.name: Course ground and collision grid
nodes.purpose: Queries the static course collision mesh: candidate selection through a uniform X-Z grid, sphere-versus-polygon depth tests, wall normal and depth rounding, plus the surface attribute and material codes the kart physics reads

nodes.name: Item economy
nodes.purpose: Tracks which of the two tandem drivers holds or stocks which item, moves items between them and between karts on contact, caps how many items may exist in the world and recycles item boxes

nodes.name: Item projectiles
nodes.purpose: Flight and steering of thrown and dropped items: gravity and ground bounce for rolling shells, a phased search-and-attack steering loop for the homing shell, star pickups that hover and rotate, and the protective heart that eats hits

nodes.name: Course traffic cars
nodes.purpose: Ambient road traffic that follows authored path points, accelerates and damps itself, and switches into damage, recover, death or wait states when a kart or an item hits it

nodes.name: CPU kart orchestration
nodes.purpose: Per-frame order of the CPU driver's body, speed and item controllers, and the rank array the CPU logic reads; the steering, speed and item brains themselves are not written at this commit

cards.name: Box mass and inertia
cards.summary: Each kart body gets its mass and diagonal inertia from the box it is shaped like, so heavier and longer bodies resist turning differently
cards.behavior: Body setup takes the four half-extents of the kart's box and builds two numbers from them. The mass is the product of all four extents scaled by eight, which is the volume of a box whose sides are twice those extents. That mass is then divided by twelve and multiplied by four to give an inertia coefficient, and each axis of the inertia diagonal is that coefficient weighted by the other two extents squared. The result is a solid-box inertia tensor kept as a diagonal, so a body that is long in one direction resists yaw more than one that is tall. The contact solver later inverts those diagonal terms into a full three by three mass matrix at the contact offset, so the same numbers that decide the mass decide how much a hit spins a kart instead of shoving it. Because the mass is derived rather than authored, a kart that has been shrunk keeps a proportional inertia and still turns like a small version of itself.

constants.name: boxVolumeFactor
constants.unit: dimensionless volume multiplier, applied once per body setup

constants.name: inertiaMassDivisor
constants.unit: dimensionless divisor, applied once per body setup

constants.name: inertiaAxisFactor
constants.unit: dimensionless multiplier, applied once per body setup

constants.name: inverseMassUnit
constants.unit: dimensionless reciprocal, recomputed every contact solve

cards.name: Gravity selection and slope assist
cards.summary: Four gravity values are picked from the kart's state flags, and part of that gravity is redirected along the ground normal to keep fast karts planted
cards.behavior: Every update the body asks which gravity to use. A kart in a knocked-about state gets the strongest pull, a kart flagged as launching or hovering uses a lighter one, other temporary states use a third value, and everything else falls back to the value stored on the body. The gravity is multiplied by the mass before it becomes a vertical force, so the two are never applied separately. A separate assist fires when the kart is moving fast, its own up axis has tilted past a small dot-product threshold and at least one wheel is touching: instead of pulling straight down, a fraction of gravity is pushed back along the body's up axis, which is what stops a strongly banked kart from peeling off the surface. A lighter version of the same assist, horizontal only, is added for a kart flagged as airborne but still in contact. The accumulated steering torque buffers are cleared whenever the assist fires, so a stale input does not fight the correction.

constants.name: knockedGravity
constants.unit: world units per update of vertical acceleration, applied every physics update

constants.name: lightGravity
constants.unit: world units per update of vertical acceleration, applied every physics update

constants.name: stateGravity
constants.unit: world units per update of vertical acceleration, applied every physics update

constants.name: slopeAssistShare
constants.unit: fraction of gravity redirected per update

constants.name: slopeAssistSpeedGate

constants.name: slopeAssistUpDotGate
constants.unit: unitless dot product with world up, sampled every physics update

cards.name: Force and torque integration
cards.summary: Accumulated forces become linear velocity, accumulated torque becomes angular velocity through a half-step split, and the result is damped before it moves the pose
cards.behavior: Forces gathered during the update are divided by the body mass and added straight into velocity. Torque is handled differently: it is rotated into body space, solved against the inertia diagonal, split by half into the angular velocity, then the second half is applied after a correction term, which is the usual way to keep a semi-implicit integrator stable when angular rates are large. A control step then damps the angular velocity by a fixed fraction unless the kart is in one of the states that must not be damped. The angular velocity is converted back to world space, the force and torque buffers are zeroed for the next update, and the pose matrix is rebuilt from the body vectors so the render transform follows the physics rather than the input. Because the damping is applied once per update rather than scaled by elapsed time, the settle time after a wall hit is fixed to the update rate.

constants.name: torqueHalfStep
constants.unit: dimensionless divisor per physics update

constants.name: angularDampingFraction
constants.unit: fraction of angular velocity kept per physics update

cards.name: Ground impulse and rolling friction
cards.summary: A wheel touching the ground receives an impulse along the contact normal, capped in the vertical direction, plus a friction impulse clamped inside a cone
cards.behavior: For a wheel contact the code measures the approach speed along the surface normal, subtracts a friction share of it, and only pushes when the remainder is positive. The push follows the normal, except that its vertical component is held under a cap unless the kart is in a state that wants a bigger pop, which is what makes a hard landing bounce slightly instead of launching. When the contact also carries a friction coefficient, the solver builds the contact mass matrix at the wheel offset, inverts it and solves for the impulse that cancels tangential slip, then clamps that impulse inside a circle whose radius is the coefficient squared, so a slippery surface simply cannot deliver a large tangential push. Velocity and angular velocity are both nudged by the applied impulse and both are scaled slightly up afterwards, which keeps a kart from sinking into a seam between polygons. The same routine finishes by recomputing the kart's speed control target from its top speed divided by a little over two, so a collision bleeds the target the throttle is chasing rather than the raw input.

constants.name: verticalImpulseCap
constants.unit: world units per update of vertical impulse, applied per contact

constants.name: postContactScale
constants.unit: dimensionless multiplier per contact

constants.name: dryGroundFrictionShare
constants.unit: fraction of normal approach speed removed per contact

constants.name: slickGroundFrictionShare
constants.unit: fraction of normal approach speed removed per contact

constants.name: contactSpeedDivisor
constants.unit: dimensionless divisor per contact

cards.name: Wall reflection and impact windows
cards.summary: A wall pushes the kart back along its normal, and whether that counts as a head-on or a glancing hit depends on speed and on the angle between the hull and the wall
cards.behavior: Wall handling reflects the kart's velocity across the wall normal and applies the result at the contact point, so an off-centre hit also spins the kart. Above a speed threshold and an angle threshold the hit raises an impact effect, and the same angle is divided by a fixed value to drive how loud that impact sounds. The angle between the kart's forward axis and the wall normal is then compared against two windows: while the kart is moving fast only impacts inside a narrower pair of bounds count as a genuine head-on, and once the kart has slowed the window widens. The narrow window is roughly sixty to a hundred and twenty degrees and the wide one roughly twenty to a hundred and sixty. That widening is why a slow scrape along a barrier still registers while the same contact at speed on a straight does not, and it is also what stops repeated retriggering when a kart is pinned against geometry.

constants.name: wallEffectSpeedGate
constants.unit: world units of speed, compared every physics update

constants.name: wallEffectAngleGate
constants.unit: degrees, compared every physics update

constants.name: impactLoudnessDivisor
constants.unit: degrees per unit, evaluated per impact

constants.unit: radians, evaluated per impact

constants.name: slowWindowLow
constants.unit: radians, evaluated per impact

cards.name: Kart versus kart bumps
cards.summary: A heavier kart shoves a lighter one harder, invulnerable karts multiply their shove, and side-on hits trade a large horizontal impulse for a tiny vertical one
cards.behavior: Before any bounce is computed the code decides whether one kart should simply win the exchange, testing an ordered list of states: invulnerability, accumulated damage, a grab state, a shrink state and a scale state. If no winner is found, the two bodies' mass terms are divided into a pair of ratios, each floored at one and raised by half again when it exceeds one, so the heavier kart always carries a multiplier. Two special cases override the ratios with large fixed values, one for an invulnerable kart and one for a shrunken kart, and both bypass the ordinary path. When the contact is side-on, meaning the impact vector sits inside a band around perpendicular, the karts receive a strike impulse proportional to the mass ratio times a base value, capped, with only a tenth of it applied vertically, which is what makes a side check push a kart sideways rather than popping it up. Otherwise the impulse is the closing speed minus a friction share, floored so that even a nudge registers, and the rumble strength is quantised into twelve steps so the pad feedback tracks the impulse coarsely rather than buzzing continuously.

constants.name: massRatioBoost
constants.unit: dimensionless multiplier per bump

constants.name: invulnerableRatio

constants.name: sideHitAngleLow
constants.unit: degrees, evaluated per bump

constants.name: sideHitAngleHigh
constants.unit: degrees, evaluated per bump

constants.unit: world units per update per mass ratio, applied per bump

constants.name: strikeImpulseCap
constants.unit: world units per update, applied per bump

constants.name: strikeVerticalShare
constants.unit: fraction of the strike applied vertically per bump

constants.name: minimumBumpImpulse

cards.name: Solver and smoothing primitives
cards.summary: The shared numeric helpers: a three by three elimination solve, a fast reciprocal square root, and ramps that chase a target with a fixed fraction or an eased one
cards.behavior: Contact resolution needs to solve a small dense system every time a wheel or a kart touches something, so the maths layer wraps a pivoting decomposition with forward and back substitution behind a single call, always at order three. Square roots go through the hardware reciprocal estimate multiplied back through the value, which is fast and accurate enough for impulse magnitudes. Angle work converts a cartesian offset into a length-elevation-azimuth triple, and the reverse direction feeds the angle through a sine and cosine table indexed by scaling a degree value into a quarter-turn table size. Two smoothing helpers are used wherever a value has to chase a target: one adds a fixed fraction of the remaining error and snaps to zero inside a tiny dead zone, while the other eases with a fraction that grows as the fourth power of elapsed steps, so the beginning of a transition is soft and the end is quick.

constants.name: solverOrder
constants.unit: matrix dimension, per solve

constants.name: smoothingDeadZone
constants.unit: value units, applied every smoothing update

constants.name: angleTableSize
constants.unit: table entries per quarter turn, applied per conversion

constants.name: halfTurnDegrees
constants.unit: degrees per conversion

constants.name: quarterTurnDegrees
constants.unit: degrees per conversion

constants.name: piApproximation

cards.name: Surface dependent top speed
cards.summary: Top speed is chosen from the surface under the wheels, and wading or splashing through water cuts it hard
cards.behavior: Top speed is not one number per kart but a lookup on the surface attribute under the body: each attribute maps to a different authored speed ceiling held on the kart, so the same driver has a different ceiling on tarmac, on a loose surface and on a low-grip surface. Two modifiers sit on top of the chosen ceiling. If the surface reports a splash height and the kart's hull is below it, the ceiling is scaled down, which is what makes a puddle or a shallow flooded stretch cost speed. If the surface is water the ceiling is compared against the water line: a kart barely submerged keeps most of its speed, while a kart submerged past a deep threshold keeps less than a third of it. Because both the surface attribute and the water line are re-read every update, the penalty appears and clears as the kart crosses an edge instead of being latched at entry.

constants.name: splashSpeedScale
constants.unit: multiplier on top speed, applied every update

constants.name: shallowWaterSpeedScale
constants.unit: multiplier on top speed, applied every update

constants.name: deepWaterSpeedScale
constants.unit: multiplier on top speed, applied every update

constants.name: deepWaterDepthGate
constants.unit: world units below the water line, sampled every update

cards.name: Down-slope bonus
cards.summary: Pointing downhill past a small dead zone adds acceleration, and past a larger angle it also raises the speed ceiling, both saturating at a clamp angle
cards.behavior: The kart's pitch relative to world up becomes a signed number whose magnitude is the slope angle. Only negative values, meaning the nose points downhill while the kart is not perfectly flat, earn anything. For acceleration the angle is first compared against a small dead zone, under which the multiplier is exactly one; past it the angle is clamped at a much larger value and remapped into a fraction, and the returned multiplier is that fraction scaled by a fifth and added to one. For speed a second, smaller pair of thresholds applies: under the lower one the bonus is zero, at the clamp it reaches the maximum, and the bonus is linear in between. The two use different angles on purpose, so a gentle down-slope that already helps a kart accelerate has not yet started raising its ceiling. Both are pure functions of the current pose, so neither lags the moment the kart crests a hill.

constants.unit: radians, sampled every update

constants.name: slopeAccClampAngle
constants.unit: radians, sampled every update

cards.name: Full and half spin-outs
cards.summary: A spin target angle is chosen from the side the hit came from, then the angular rate ramps up and eases as the body reaches two turns or one
cards.behavior: Both spin variants read the lateral part of the accumulated impulse to pick which way to rotate, fall back to the steering angle when that is exactly zero, and then enter a state that drives the yaw rate towards a full turn target. The full spin aims at two complete turns, the half spin at one. While the accumulated angle is small the rate gains a large increment per update; once it passes a coarse threshold the increments shrink, so the tail of the spin settles onto the target instead of slamming into it. When the accumulated angle passes a completion threshold slightly under the target the wheel angular rates are zeroed, the spin flags are cleared and the kart returns to driving. Because the target is an absolute angle rather than a timer, a kart nudged into a wall mid-spin keeps the rotation it has already banked, and the same routine serves both the ordinary spin and the shorter half spin, which is why the half spin reaches its threshold and unwinds sooner.

cards.name: Thrown, bombed and frozen
cards.summary: Hazards that remove control launch the kart upward with an impulse scaled by the hazard's power, and each hazard type has its own recovery timing
cards.behavior: A thrower-style hazard reports a power value; the crash routine multiplies it by two hundred and by the kart's mass and injects that straight into the vertical force buffer, so a heavy kart is thrown as high as a light one rather than less. The same entry point seeds a small negative pitch rate, zeroes the spin and slope buffers, raises the launched flag and marks the kart as crashing so steering input is ignored. A bomb does the same with a much larger fixed vertical impulse and a positive pitch rate, which is why a bomb sends a kart up and forward rather than up and back. The freeze variant takes a different route: it stops the driver animation outright, raises a frozen flag, aborts any item roulette the victim was spinning and shuts off their exhaust effect for the duration before unwinding through its own state machine. Every entry point also starts a short grace timer so the victim cannot be hit again the moment it lands.

constants.name: throwerImpulseScale
constants.unit: world units per update per unit of hazard power

constants.name: bombImpulse
constants.unit: world units per update of vertical impulse

cards.name: Star invulnerability window
cards.summary: A star grants a fixed countdown of invulnerability that is shorter in the escape battle mode
cards.behavior: Entering the star state raises an invulnerable flag on the body, plays a state change on the kart's material animation and starts a countdown. The countdown takes one of two fixed lengths: the shorter value is used in the escape battle mode where a tighter power window keeps the round moving, and the longer value everywhere else. Each update simply decrements, and when it reaches zero the flag is cleared and the material animation is stopped, returning the kart to ordinary collision rules. During the window the kart counts as a winner in kart-versus-kart contacts, so the mass ratio logic hands it a much larger shove and it never receives one itself, and it also ignores item reactions that would otherwise spin it.

constants.name: starFramesNormal
constants.unit: frames at 60 Hz

constants.name: starFramesEscape
constants.unit: frames at 60 Hz

cards.name: Thunder shrink and recovery
cards.summary: The thunder item shrinks every other kart to half scale for a fixed window, then a two stage recovery shakes it back to full size
cards.behavior: When the item fires it walks every kart in the race and skips any that is already shrunken, invulnerable, inside a cannon or otherwise immune. Each valid target is flagged, force spun, made to drop its items, given a rumble motor and a voice cue, and put on a countdown starting from a shake scale of one. During the shrink phase the scale eases towards a half, and once the countdown has burned all but the final half second the state moves to waiting. At zero the recovery cue plays and the scale eases back towards one; the shake phase then decays a tiny amplitude to nothing while a sine wave with a fixed increment drives the scale around one, and only when the amplitude is exhausted is the flag cleared, the shadow restored and the kart handed back to normal rules. The same object exposes a scale that the physics layer multiplies the inertia diagonal by, so a shrunken kart both looks and spins like a smaller body.

constants.unit: frames at 60 Hz

constants.unit: frames at 60 Hz counted down, checked every update

cards.name: Damage lockout timers
cards.summary: Four damage reactions each hold the driver for a different number of frames, and the two biggest ones also shake the camera
cards.behavior: Reactions are chosen from the severity of the hit: a short one for ordinary bumps, a medium one for half strength hits, a long one for burns, and the longest for the big hit that follows a bomb or a heavy impact. Each sets a state and a countdown; while the countdown runs the driver animation is forced into the reaction and steering input is ignored. When it expires the reaction flag is cleared and a release animation plays, so the kart visibly settles before control comes back. The two larger reactions also ask the camera looking at that kart for a shake, which is why a bomb reads as a big event even when the victim is off to the side of the screen. A protection window suppresses all of it, so a kart that is already in one does not accumulate further lockouts.

cards.name: Chase camera placement and mode choice
cards.summary: The per kart camera picks a mode every update and frames the kart from an authored anchor pushed along its forward direction
cards.behavior: Each update the camera resolves which of a dozen or more modes applies, testing in order whether the kart is hanging after a fall, dropping, launching, landing, entering a pipe, reversing, in a start or finish demo, in a replay, or simply driving; only the ordinary driving case reaches the free chase mode. For the authored modes the camera reads a camera record for the area the kart is in, takes the record's position and pushes it a fixed distance along the record's own forward direction, which is how over-the-shoulder and roadside shots are built from level data rather than from the kart pose. The pure chase mode instead lifts an anchor a fixed height above the kart and keeps the distance from that anchor to the authored camera, effectively rotating the authored offset with the kart. The search and path variants reuse the same record and the same push, differing only in whether the anchor starts at the record or at the kart, which is why every mode lines up with the authored framing when the camera cuts between them.

constants.name: framingPushDistance
constants.unit: world units along the record forward direction, applied per placement

constants.name: chaseAnchorHeight
constants.unit: world units above the kart origin, applied per placement

cards.name: Sector progress and lap counting
cards.summary: Position becomes a fraction between two checkpoint planes, and that fraction accumulates into race progress with wrap handling and a reverse-drive test
cards.behavior: Each sector is bounded by two checkpoint planes. A kart's planar position is tested against the sector's left and right bounds with cross products in the ground plane, and if it is inside, the fractional distance is the distance from the entry plane divided by the sum of the distances to both planes, clamped so that a hair-thin negative result collapses to zero. That fraction is scaled by the share of total track length the sector covers and offset by the track that lies before it, giving a progression within one lap. The difference from the previous update is taken, and any jump larger than half a lap is corrected by a whole lap in the appropriate direction, which is what makes crossing the start line and driving back over it both behave sensibly. Accumulated race progress is floored at a negative limit so a kart driving the wrong way for a long time cannot underflow the comparison used for ranking. A lap only completes when the sector pass set is complete and the accumulated progress has exceeded the recorded lap count, so cutting across the infield no longer counts. Reverse driving is detected independently by dotting the kart's forward axis against the sector's backward normal.

constants.name: lapWrapNegativeThreshold
constants.unit: fraction of a lap per update

constants.name: lapWrapCorrection
constants.unit: fraction of a lap, applied per wrap

constants.name: progressFloor
constants.unit: laps of accumulated progress

constants.name: velocityToTimeScale
constants.unit: world units per update converted to per frame distance, applied once per lap completion

constants.name: reverseDotThreshold
constants.unit: unitless dot product, sampled every update

constants.name: fractionalClamp
constants.unit: fraction of a sector, applied per query

cards.name: Race ranking pass
cards.summary: Ranks are assigned from the outside in: finished karts by time from the top, running karts by remaining distance from the bottom
cards.behavior: The ranking pass runs a two ended sweep. On each iteration it scans every still unranked kart and keeps two candidates: the finished kart with the earliest total time, or where no time is available the one that crossed the goal on the earliest frame, and the running kart with the smallest remaining distance to its next checkpoint. The distance comparison starts from a large constant so a candidate is always found while at least one kart remains. The finished candidate takes the next rank from the top and the running candidate takes the next rank from the bottom, and the loop walks inward until the two ends meet. That is why a kart finishing while others still race slots in ahead of everyone, and why the rest of the field is ordered purely by track progress. Battle modes run their own passes that rank on balloons, robberies or bomb points instead of distance.

constants.name: distanceSearchInitialBound
constants.unit: world units of remaining track distance, initialised each rank pass

cards.name: Item box recycling and world item budget
cards.summary: Boxes stay inactive for a fixed time after being taken, and the number of items alive at once is capped per kind and per mode
cards.behavior: A box that is hit switches to an inactive state and counts up; while the count is under the configured rest time it stays invisible and cannot be taken, and once it passes the box opens again and returns to the pool. The rest time is a single stored value that a mode may override before play starts, so a battle mode can cycle boxes faster than a race. Separately the manager keeps per kind caps on how many of an item may exist and how many may move at once, plus a running budget on the total number of moving items in the world, evicting by priority whenever a new one would exceed it. Bomb battle raises the per kind and total caps far above their race values, because a battle run with the ordinary caps would starve. Item selection is handled by a shuffle object per kart and per driver, and karts whose driver is one of the two special ones are handed a different shuffle implementation reserved for the special racers.

cards.name: Rolling shell flight
cards.summary: A thrown shell leaves the hand with the thrower's velocity added, falls under its own gravity, bounces along the ground and dies after a limited number of wall hits
cards.behavior: On release the shell's direction comes from the thrower's hand matrix, is scaled to a launch speed and then has the thrower's own velocity added, so a shell thrown from a fast kart travels faster. A horizontal stick contribution is folded in unless the throw is the backwards variant, which simply flips the horizontal components. While flying the shell adds its gravity to vertical velocity each update, integrates position, snaps itself to ground height plus a height offset when it would sink below it, and reflects the vertical velocity with a small loss while redirecting the horizontal velocity along the ground normal so it follows a banked surface. A cap on total speed keeps a shell from accelerating without limit down a long slope. Every wall contact increments a counter, and when that counter reaches its limit the shell is teleported back to where it entered the world and removed, which bounds its life without an explicit timer. Special variants get twice the wall allowance, and a freshly released shell is given a short no collision window so it can clear the kart that threw it.

constants.name: shellGravity
constants.unit: world units per update of vertical acceleration, applied every update

cards.name: Homing shell steering
cards.summary: The flying shell waits, follows a path while hunting, chases a target from an offset behind it, then commits to a straight final dive
cards.behavior: The homing shell runs a small state machine. It first rides along on its owner's velocity, losing vertical speed, until a short wait window ends. It then follows authored path points, steering towards the next point with a fixed added velocity and shedding speed each update. Once it has a target, the search state aims at the target's horizontal position, adds a steering velocity, matches the target's own speed when the target is close and slows instead while still far away. If a full search window passes without resolving, it flips into an attack state where it commits to a straight line towards the target, accelerates along it, caps its speed and expires after its own attack window. A small angle comparison decides whether the shell snaps to a new direction matrix or blends between old and new headings, so a shell already pointing the right way does not visibly wobble.

cards.name: Ambient traffic behaviour
cards.summary: Road traffic accelerates towards a target point, damps itself, and swaps into damage and recovery states when something hits it
cards.behavior: Each traffic car owns a target position derived from an authored path point. Every update it steers towards that target with a handle power, adds an acceleration value while below its intended speed, and applies an air resistance fraction everywhere above it, which gives the cars their glide and their soft speed ceiling. Gravity applies separately while a car is off the ground, with a lighter value used in the damaged state so a knocked car floats longer than it should before settling. A horn check compares distance and facing between a kart and the car, so a warning only plays from vehicles actually ahead of the player and pointing the same way. Collisions are resolved against karts and against items, and a hit redirects the car into a damage state whose velocity is seeded from the impact; from there it runs through recover, death and wait states before returning to path following.

cards.name: Driver and vehicle attributes
cards.summary: Driver records carry a weight class and a default partner, vehicle records carry a weight class and a wheel count, and both are resolved through lookup switches
cards.behavior: Two small record types hold everything the rest of the code asks about a driver or a vehicle. A driver record pairs an identity with a partner identity, a weight class, a default vehicle and two small flags; a vehicle record pairs an identity with a weight class, a wheel count, a small offset and the driver it belongs to. Lookups are switches over the identity enumerations returning pointers into static tables, so a query costs a branch and never an allocation. The weight class is exposed as a plain integer for drivers and as an enumeration for vehicles, and the wheel count is the only place where the six-wheeled bodies differ structurally from the four-wheeled ones. Anything that needs a kart's physical character reads these tables indirectly, which is why a pairing that puts a light driver in a heavy vehicle ends up handling like the vehicle rather than the driver.

cards.name: Ground and wall query
cards.summary: Collision is found by walking a uniform grid of candidate polygons around the kart and taking the deepest sphere intersection, with grazing depth rounding so contacts do not chatter
cards.behavior: A query starts from the kart's current and previous positions plus a radius that together describe a moving sphere. Dynamic objects are tested first so a moving platform or a crate can take priority over the static mesh. For the static mesh the query turns the sphere footprint into a grid aligned rectangle, converts that rectangle into grid indices through the course's own world to grid mapping, rejects indices outside the grid with a tiny tolerance, and then walks the candidate cells. Each candidate polygon is tested for a sphere intersection and the best depth is kept along with its normal, attribute and material. Finally the depth is rounded: when the contact normal and the incoming movement direction are nearly parallel the depth is replaced by a small constant instead of the computed value, which is what stops a kart sliding along a wall from being reported as deeply penetrating and bounced over and over.
